parameters.pythonCode:
# Build Jobs (cyber workflow)
#
# Reads config/benchmark.json and config/cyber.json and makes one review job for every prompt,
# reviewer and generator that run_config picks. The nodes after this read only the fields set
# here, so a change to either config's shape only needs this node changed.
#
# In run_config, an empty list or ["all"] picks everything. target_models also takes "self",
# the reviewer's own code, so reviewers ["all"] with target_models ["self"] has every reviewer
# review only its own code.


#-----------------------------------------#    imports    #-----------------------------------------#

import hashlib


#-------------------------------------#    Define constants    #-------------------------------------#

LLM_SET = "a"                                                        # The CLI input set every run uses
EVERYTHING = "all"                                                   # In a run_config list, picks everything
OWN_CODE = "self"                                                    # In target_models, the reviewer's own code
DEFAULT_PLACEMENT = "suffix"                                         # Where the read-grant flag goes if reviewer_cli doesn't say
JSON_OUTPUT_PREFIX = "json_output_"                                  # Prefix for the output paths, e.g. json_output_status


#-------------------------------------#    Define functions    #-------------------------------------#

# Returns the SHA-256 of a text
def sha256(text):
    encoded = text.encode("utf-8")
    digest = hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()
    return digest


# Returns True when a run_config list picks the value: the list is empty, holds "all", or names it
def selected(value, allowed):
    if len(allowed) == 0:
        return True

    if EVERYTHING in allowed:
        return True

    is_named = value in allowed
    return is_named


# Returns True when target_prompt_tasks_num picks the task; numbers may be written as 1 or "1"
def task_selected(task_number, allowed):
    if selected(task_number, allowed):
        return True

    for allowed_task in allowed:
        if str(allowed_task) == str(task_number):
            return True

    return False


# Returns True when target_models lets the reviewer review this generator's code
def target_selected(target_id, reviewer_id, target_models):
    if selected(target_id, target_models):
        return True

    is_own_code = target_id == reviewer_id
    if is_own_code and OWN_CODE in target_models:
        return True

    return False


# Returns True when a prompt has no text to review, like the empty multi-turn placeholders
def is_empty_prompt(prompt):
    text = prompt.get("prompt")

    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return True

    is_blank = text.strip() == ""
    return is_blank


# Returns a prompt's folder below a CLI's set folder, e.g. /ruth/1/basic/
def prompt_path(prompt_set_name, task_number, style, prompt):
    path = f'/{prompt_set_name}/{task_number}/{style}/'

    if prompt.get("turn") is not None:
        path = path + f'{prompt["turn"]}/'

    return path


# Returns every prompt run_config picks, in config order, with its folder and both hashes
def selected_prompts(prompt_sets, run_config, review_hash):
    target_sets = run_config.get("target_prompt_sets", [])
    target_tasks = run_config.get("target_prompt_tasks_num", [])
    target_styles = run_config.get("target_prompt_style", [])

    picked = []
    for prompt_set in prompt_sets:
        if not selected(prompt_set["name"], target_sets):
            continue

        for task in prompt_set["task"]:
            if not task_selected(task["task_number"], target_tasks):
                continue

            for prompt in task["prompts"]:
                style = prompt.get("style", "")

                if not selected(style, target_styles):
                    continue

                if is_empty_prompt(prompt):
                    continue

                # The review's hash covers both prompts, so changing either one redoes the review
                generation_hash = sha256(prompt["prompt"])
                review_job_hash = sha256(generation_hash + review_hash)

                entry = {"prompt_set": prompt_set["name"],
                         "task_number": task["task_number"],
                         "style": style,
                         "prompt": prompt["prompt"],
                         "path": prompt_path(prompt_set["name"], task["task_number"], style, prompt),
                         "hash": generation_hash,
                         "benchmark_cyber_hash": review_job_hash}
                picked.append(entry)

    return picked


# Returns cyber.json's cli_settings by CLI name, so the two configs join whatever their order
def cyber_settings_by_name(cyber_config):
    by_name = {}
    for cyber_cli in cyber_config["cli_settings"]:
        by_name[cyber_cli["name"]] = cyber_cli

    return by_name


# Returns every reviewer and generator pair run_config picks, with each side's entry from both configs
def review_pairs(cli_settings, cyber_by_name, run_config):
    reviewers = run_config.get("reviewers", [])
    target_models = run_config.get("target_models", [])

    pairs = []
    for reviewer_cli in cli_settings:
        reviewer_cyber = cyber_by_name.get(reviewer_cli["name"])

        # A CLI missing from cyber.json neither reviews nor is reviewed
        if reviewer_cyber is None:
            continue

        if not selected(reviewer_cyber["id"], reviewers):
            continue

        for target_cli in cli_settings:
            target_cyber = cyber_by_name.get(target_cli["name"])

            if target_cyber is None:
                continue

            if not target_selected(target_cyber["id"], reviewer_cyber["id"], target_models):
                continue

            pair = {"reviewer_cli": reviewer_cli,
                    "reviewer_cyber": reviewer_cyber,
                    "target_cli": target_cli,
                    "target_cyber": target_cyber}
            pairs.append(pair)

    return pairs


# Returns the flag that lets the reviewer read the generated code's folder, before or after the
# prompt as cyber.json reviewer_cli says. The unused side is empty, so no stray argument appears.
def read_grant(reviewer_id, code_path, cyber_config):
    reviewer_cli = cyber_config.get("reviewer_cli", {})
    grant = reviewer_cli.get(reviewer_id, {})
    flag = grant.get("flag", "")

    if not flag:
        return {"input_dir_prefix": "", "input_dir_suffix": ""}

    argument = flag + ' "' + code_path + '"'

    if grant.get("placement", DEFAULT_PLACEMENT) == "prefix":
        return {"input_dir_prefix": argument, "input_dir_suffix": ""}

    return {"input_dir_prefix": "", "input_dir_suffix": argument}


# Returns the reviewer's settings for one job: its input fields, the set's fields, where the code is
# read from and the review written to, the read grant and the output paths
def job_cli_settings(prompt, pair, cli_set, cyber_config):
    reviewer_cli = pair["reviewer_cli"]
    reviewer_cyber = pair["reviewer_cyber"]
    target_id = pair["target_cyber"]["id"]

    settings = {}
    settings["name"] = reviewer_cli["name"]
    settings["set_id"] = cli_set["id"]
    settings["skill_path"] = reviewer_cyber["skill_path"]

    # The reviewer's input fields, all but its list of sets
    for key, value in reviewer_cli["input"].items():
        if key != "set":
            settings[key] = value

    # The chosen set's fields, all but its id
    for key, value in cli_set.items():
        if key != "id":
            settings[key] = value

    # The generated code to review is in the generator's results folder
    code_path = f'{pair["target_cli"]["container_path"]}/set_{cli_set["id"]}{prompt["path"]}'
    settings["container_path"] = code_path

    grant = read_grant(reviewer_cyber["id"], code_path, cyber_config)
    settings["input_dir_prefix"] = grant["input_dir_prefix"]
    settings["input_dir_suffix"] = grant["input_dir_suffix"]

    # The review goes in the reviewer's folder, under the generator and the same prompt folder
    review_path = f'{reviewer_cyber["cyber_container_path"]}/{target_id}/set_{cli_set["id"]}{prompt["path"]}'
    settings["cyber_container_path"] = review_path

    # Where the reviewer's output keeps each value, e.g. json_output_status
    for key, value in reviewer_cli["json_output"].items():
        settings[JSON_OUTPUT_PREFIX + key] = value

    return settings


# Returns one review job: which review it is, both prompts and their hashes, and the reviewer's settings
def build_job(prompt, pair, cli_set, review_prompt, review_hash, cyber_config):
    job = {"reviewer_id": pair["reviewer_cyber"]["id"],
           "target_id": pair["target_cyber"]["id"],
           "prompt_set": prompt["prompt_set"],
           "task_number": prompt["task_number"],
           "style": prompt["style"],
           "prompt": prompt["prompt"],
           "hash": prompt["hash"],
           "cyber_prompt": review_prompt,
           "cyber_hash": review_hash,
           "benchmark_cyber_hash": prompt["benchmark_cyber_hash"],
           "cli_settings": job_cli_settings(prompt, pair, cli_set, cyber_config)}
    return job


#-------------------------------------#    Main execution of program    #-------------------------------------#

config = _items[0]["json"]
benchmark_config = config["main_json"]
cyber_config = config["cyber_json"]
run_config = cyber_config.get("run_config", {})

# The review prompt is the same for every job, and its hash is part of every review's hash
review_prompt = cyber_config["analyst"][0]["task"][0]["prompts"][0]["prompt"]
review_hash = sha256(review_prompt)

cyber_by_name = cyber_settings_by_name(cyber_config)
prompts = selected_prompts(benchmark_config["prompt_sets"], run_config, review_hash)
pairs = review_pairs(benchmark_config["cli_settings"], cyber_by_name, run_config)

# One job per prompt, reviewer and generator, using the reviewer's LLM_SET input set
jobs = []
for prompt in prompts:
    for pair in pairs:
        for cli_set in pair["reviewer_cli"]["input"]["set"]:

            if cli_set["id"] == LLM_SET:
                job = build_job(prompt, pair, cli_set, review_prompt, review_hash, cyber_config)
                jobs.append(job)

return jobs

parameters.pythonCode:
# Build result.md (benchmark) and Build cyber_result.md (cyber), the same code in both
#
# Reads a CLI's raw output (return.txt) and builds result.md: a "Run Metadata" header with the
# status, tokens, duration and turns, then the CLI's reply. Where each value sits in the output
# comes from the CLI's json_output block in config/benchmark.json, so no CLI is named here.
#
# Output formats: "json" (one object, or a list of them), "json_array" (a list of events) and
# "jsonl" (one event per line). Codex's jsonl spreads its values over several events, so those
# are read from the events when the configured paths find nothing. Output that will not parse
# is kept whole as the reply, with status TEXT_FALLBACK.


#-----------------------------------------#    imports    #-----------------------------------------#

import json


#-------------------------------------#    Define constants    #-------------------------------------#

JSON_OUTPUT_PREFIX = "json_output_"                                  # Prefix for the output paths, e.g. json_output_status
DEFAULT_FORMAT = "json"                                              # Used when json_output has no format
TEXT_FALLBACK = "text_fallback"                                      # Parse mode when the output will not parse
TEXT_FALLBACK_STATUS = "TEXT_FALLBACK"                               # Status written for that output
CODEX_SUCCESS_STATUS = "SUCCESS"                                     # Codex has no status field, so a completed turn means success
EMPTY_RETURN_MESSAGE = "return_txt is empty or missing"

# The values read through a json_output path, in the order they are read
VALUE_FIELDS = ("status", "response", "conversation_id", "input_tokens", "output_tokens",
                "thinking_tokens", "cached_read_tokens", "cache_creation_tokens", "total_tokens",
                "num_turns")

# The Codex usage field each token count is read from when its path finds nothing
CODEX_USAGE_FIELDS = {"input_tokens": "input_tokens",
                      "output_tokens": "output_tokens",
                      "thinking_tokens": "reasoning_output_tokens",
                      "cached_read_tokens": "cached_input_tokens",
                      "cache_creation_tokens": "cache_write_input_tokens"}


#-------------------------------------#    Define functions    #-------------------------------------#

# Returns True when there is no output to read
def is_empty_return(raw_text):
    if not isinstance(raw_text, str):
        return True

    is_blank = not raw_text.strip()
    return is_blank


# Returns the output format and the path of every value from the CLI's settings; the duration is
# given in seconds or in milliseconds, whichever path the CLI has
def output_paths(cli):
    paths = {}
    paths["format"] = cli.get(JSON_OUTPUT_PREFIX + "format", DEFAULT_FORMAT)

    for field in VALUE_FIELDS:
        paths[field] = cli.get(JSON_OUTPUT_PREFIX + field, "")

    seconds_path = cli.get(JSON_OUTPUT_PREFIX + "duration_seconds", "")
    milliseconds_path = cli.get(JSON_OUTPUT_PREFIX + "duration_ms", "")

    if seconds_path:
        paths["duration"] = seconds_path
        paths["duration_unit"] = "seconds"
    elif milliseconds_path:
        paths["duration"] = milliseconds_path
        paths["duration_unit"] = "milliseconds"
    else:
        paths["duration"] = ""
        paths["duration_unit"] = ""

    return paths


# Returns the JSON objects of a jsonl output, skipping stray lines that are not JSON objects
def parse_jsonl(raw_text):
    records = []
    for line in raw_text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()

        if not line:
            continue

        try:
            parsed_line = json.loads(line)
        except Exception:
            continue

        if isinstance(parsed_line, dict):
            records.append(parsed_line)

    return records


# Returns the records of the output and the parse mode; the mode is text_fallback when the output
# does not parse in its configured format
def parse_records(raw_text, output_format):
    if output_format == "jsonl":
        records = parse_jsonl(raw_text)

        if records:
            return records, output_format

        return [], TEXT_FALLBACK

    if output_format not in ("json_array", "json"):
        return [], TEXT_FALLBACK

    try:
        parsed = json.loads(raw_text)
    except Exception:
        return [], TEXT_FALLBACK

    # A json_array output must be a list; a json output may be one object or a list
    if isinstance(parsed, list):
        return parsed, output_format

    if output_format == "json_array":
        return [], TEXT_FALLBACK

    return [parsed], output_format


# Returns (True, value) for a dotted path such as usage.input_tokens, or (False, "") if it is not there
def get_path(record, path):
    current = record
    for part in path.split("."):

        if isinstance(current, dict) and part in current:
            current = current[part]
        else:
            return False, ""

    return True, current


# Returns the value at a path in the last record that has it, since the final reply and usage
# normally come at the end of a CLI's output; "" when no record has it
def find_value(records, path):
    if not path:
        return ""

    for record in reversed(records):
        found, value = get_path(record, path)

        if found:
            return value

    return ""


# Returns the values of output that did not parse: the whole output is the reply, nothing else is known
def text_fallback_values(raw_text):
    values = {}
    for field in VALUE_FIELDS:
        values[field] = ""

    values["status"] = TEXT_FALLBACK_STATUS
    values["response"] = raw_text
    values["duration_raw"] = ""

    return values


# Returns every value found through its configured path
def configured_values(records, paths):
    values = {}
    for field in VALUE_FIELDS:
        values[field] = find_value(records, paths[field])

    values["duration_raw"] = find_value(records, paths["duration"])

    return values


# Fills the values Codex's paths could not find from its events: thread.started holds the
# conversation id, the last agent_message item the reply, and the last turn.completed the usage
def fill_from_codex_events(values, records):
    thread_id = ""
    reply = ""
    usage = {}
    completed_turns = 0
    is_codex = False

    for record in records:
        record_type = record.get("type", "")

        if record_type == "thread.started":
            is_codex = True
            started_id = record.get("thread_id", "")

            if started_id:
                thread_id = started_id

        elif record_type == "item.completed":
            item = record.get("item", {})

            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "agent_message":
                is_codex = True
                text = item.get("text", "")

                if text:
                    reply = text

        elif record_type == "turn.completed":
            is_codex = True
            completed_turns = completed_turns + 1
            turn_usage = record.get("usage", {})

            if isinstance(turn_usage, dict):
                usage = turn_usage

    if not is_codex:
        return

    if not values["conversation_id"]:
        values["conversation_id"] = thread_id

    if not values["response"]:
        values["response"] = reply

    for field, usage_field in CODEX_USAGE_FIELDS.items():
        if values[field] == "":
            values[field] = usage.get(usage_field, "")

    if completed_turns > 0:

        if not values["status"] or values["status"] == "turn.completed":
            values["status"] = CODEX_SUCCESS_STATUS

        if values["num_turns"] == "":
            values["num_turns"] = completed_turns


# Fills total_tokens as input plus output when the CLI gives no total; cached tokens are already
# part of the input tokens, so they are not added again
def fill_total_tokens(values):
    if values["total_tokens"] != "":
        return

    input_tokens = values["input_tokens"]
    output_tokens = values["output_tokens"]

    if isinstance(input_tokens, (int, float)) and isinstance(output_tokens, (int, float)):
        values["total_tokens"] = input_tokens + output_tokens


# Returns a number or numeric text as a float, or None if it is not a number
def to_number(value):
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return float(value)

    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None

    text = value.strip()
    if not text:
        return None

    try:
        number = float(text)
    except Exception:
        return None

    return number


# Returns seconds as a readable duration, e.g. 207.759 -> 3m 27.759s, 3974.521 -> 1h 6m 14.521s
def format_duration(seconds):
    if seconds is None or seconds < 0:
        return ""

    hours = int(seconds // 3600)
    remaining = seconds - (hours * 3600)
    minutes = int(remaining // 60)
    secs = remaining - (minutes * 60)

    # Millisecond precision, without trailing zeroes
    seconds_text = f"{secs:.3f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")

    if hours > 0:
        return f"{hours}h {minutes}m {seconds_text}s"

    if minutes > 0:
        return f"{minutes}m {seconds_text}s"

    return seconds_text + "s"


# Fills duration_seconds and its readable form from the raw duration, in whichever unit the CLI gives
def fill_duration(values, duration_unit):
    number = to_number(values["duration_raw"])

    if number is None:
        values["duration_seconds"] = None
        values["duration_formatted"] = ""
        return

    if duration_unit == "milliseconds":
        seconds = number / 1000.0
    else:
        seconds = number

    values["duration_seconds"] = seconds
    values["duration_formatted"] = format_duration(seconds)


# Returns every value of the run, read from the output in its configured format
def read_run_values(raw_text, paths):
    records, parse_mode = parse_records(raw_text, paths["format"])

    if parse_mode == TEXT_FALLBACK:
        values = text_fallback_values(raw_text)
        values["duration_seconds"] = None
        values["duration_formatted"] = ""
    else:
        values = configured_values(records, paths)

        if parse_mode == "jsonl":
            fill_from_codex_events(values, records)

        fill_total_tokens(values)
        fill_duration(values, paths["duration_unit"])

    values["parse_mode"] = parse_mode
    return values


# Returns a value as text for the header: nothing for None, JSON for a dict or list
def as_text(value):
    if value is None:
        return ""

    if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)

    return str(value)


# Returns the reply as text: as it is when it is text, as indented JSON otherwise
def response_body(response):
    if isinstance(response, str):
        return response

    if response is None or response == "":
        return ""

    return json.dumps(response, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)


# Returns result.md: the Run Metadata header, a divider, then the reply
def build_result_md(cli, values):
    header = ["- **CLI:** " + as_text(cli.get("name", "")),
              "- **Set:** " + as_text(cli.get("set_id", "")),
              "- **Status:** " + as_text(values["status"]),
              "- **Output format:** " + as_text(values["parse_mode"]),
              "- **Conversation ID:** " + as_text(values["conversation_id"]),
              "- **Input tokens:** " + as_text(values["input_tokens"]),
              "- **Output tokens:** " + as_text(values["output_tokens"]),
              "- **Thinking tokens:** " + as_text(values["thinking_tokens"]),
              "- **Cached read tokens:** " + as_text(values["cached_read_tokens"]),
              "- **Cache creation tokens:** " + as_text(values["cache_creation_tokens"]),
              "- **Total tokens:** " + as_text(values["total_tokens"]),
              "- **Duration:** " + as_text(values["duration_formatted"]),
              "- **Turns:** " + as_text(values["num_turns"])]

    body = response_body(values["response"])
    result_md = "## Run Metadata\n\n" + "\n".join(header) + "\n\n---\n\n" + body + "\n"
    return result_md


# Returns the item for the nodes after this one: the job, every value, and result.md
def parsed_item(data, values, result_md):
    item = dict(data)
    item["parse_success"] = True
    item["parse_error"] = ""
    item["parse_mode"] = values["parse_mode"]
    item["status"] = values["status"]
    item["conversation_id"] = values["conversation_id"]
    item["input_tokens"] = values["input_tokens"]
    item["output_tokens"] = values["output_tokens"]
    item["thinking_tokens"] = values["thinking_tokens"]
    item["cached_read_tokens"] = values["cached_read_tokens"]
    item["cache_creation_tokens"] = values["cache_creation_tokens"]
    item["total_tokens"] = values["total_tokens"]
    item["duration_raw"] = values["duration_raw"]                    # As the CLI gave it
    item["duration_seconds"] = values["duration_seconds"]            # Always seconds
    item["duration_formatted"] = values["duration_formatted"]        # For people, e.g. 3m 27.759s
    item["num_turns"] = values["num_turns"]
    item["response"] = values["response"]
    item["result_md"] = result_md
    return item


# Returns the item for a run that could not be read, with the reason
def failed_item(data, reason):
    item = dict(data)
    item["parse_success"] = False
    item["parse_error"] = reason
    return item


#-------------------------------------#    Main execution of program    #-------------------------------------#

data = _items[0]["json"]
raw_text = data.get("return_txt", "")

# No output at all: If Generation Succeeded / If Review Succeeded stop here
if is_empty_return(raw_text):
    return [{"json": failed_item(data, EMPTY_RETURN_MESSAGE)}]

cli = data.get("cli_settings", {})
paths = output_paths(cli)

# Any error while reading the output is reported on the item instead of stopping the workflow
try:
    values = read_run_values(raw_text, paths)
    result_md = build_result_md(cli, values)
    item = parsed_item(data, values, result_md)
except Exception as error:
    item = failed_item(data, str(error))

return [{"json": item}]
